I learned mostly by watching YouTube videos of others making it. Basically I just used two clean glass one gallon jars and rinsed them with vinegar and hot water. I brewed about two gallons of black tea and added a cup of sugar per gallon. I put it in the jars and added 1/4 cup of white vinegar to each since it was my first batch with these scobys. I shouldn't have to do that for the next batch though. Then I let the tea cool (ideally to room temp but I didn't have time). Then add the scoby, and cover with some type of cloth or coffee filter to let air in but keep bugs out. Then let it ferment for about a week (I'm still on this step), and it can be tasted by getting some in a straw below the scoby. If it's good at that point you can either refrigerate and drink as-is, or you can bottle it and add flavor like fruit or herbs or anything, I haven't gotten to that stage yet though. Once it's bottled and flavored it can ferment a couple days in the bottles and it should be done. Oh one other tip I've seen, don't use any metal on or around the scoby, it apparently reacts badly to it.
